messages:
maria.security: Heads-up — seeing envelope decryption failures in prod since ~11:40 UTC after yesterday's Azure Key Vault RBAC tightening rollout. Multiple services returned 403/503 from KV. Some requests hit local DEK cache fallback and stayed OK, but overall ~7% user-facing errors during the spike. Need immediate mitigation steps + audit artifacts for compliance. Anyone oncall?

maria.security: Example logs from the proxy layer:
```
2026-06-04T11:41:02Z service=ingest request_id=aa1b2c decryption_attempt=1 key_id=kv://projects/prod/keys/enc-01 error=403 Forbidden from AzureKeyVault endpoint=/vaults/prod-kv/decrypt
2026-06-04T11:41:03Z service=ingest request_id=aa1b2d decryption_attempt=2 key_id=kv://projects/prod/keys/enc-01 fallback=local-dek success=true
2026-06-04T11:41:05Z service=chat request_id=bb7c8d decryption_attempt=1 key_id=kv://projects/prod/keys/enc-02 error=503 ServiceUnavailable
```

dan.infra: I rolled the RBAC change out to lock down access from legacy subscription roles -> service-principal-only. Suspect conditional access policy + token renewal timing caused some managed identities to fail auth against KV. Rolling back the RBAC change now to validate.

dan.infra: Rollback command (run against subscription):
```bash
az role assignment delete --assignee <svc-princ-id> --role \"Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption\" --scope /subscriptions/0000.../resourceGroups/prod/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/prod-kv
# then recreate more specific assignments for the new principal set
```

leo.ops: We saw the upstream retry loop amplify the KV failures — a lot of parallel decrypts retried with no backoff and started hitting the vault gateway. Temporarily throttled the client-side retries and bumped DEK cache TTL to buy us time. Config change pushed to prod:
```yaml
crypto:
  dek_local_cache_ttl_seconds: 900   # increased from 60 -> 15m
  decrypt_retry_policy:
    max_attempts: 3
    base_backoff_ms: 250
    max_backoff_ms: 5000
    jitter: true
```

leo.ops: Also reduced concurrent decrypt workers on the ingest path from 50 -> 12 for the hot partition to avoid overloading KV. :grimacing:

oliver.sre: Quick mitigations we should apply now:
- keep the rollback in flight (if dan confirms)
- enable circuit breaker for 5xx/429 on KV client: open after 5 failures for 30s
- ensure DEK cache only used for non-PII routes until we validate audit logs
- add per-key fallback counters to telemetry (we need counts for compliance)

oliver.sre: Example circuit config we recommended:
```json
{\"circuit_breaker\": {\"failure_threshold\": 5, \"open_interval_seconds\": 30, \"half_open_trials\": 2}}
```

anya.prod: From compliance perspective: we need a list of affected key ARNs, timestamps of failures, which tenant/customers saw degraded responses, and confirmation that any cached DEK usage is logged and retained. SOC2 requires proof we didn't silently decrypt customer PII without an auditable trail. Please label the KV audit logs and export a copy to the secure S3 bucket.

maria.security: KMS bot reported alerts earlier:
kms-bot: ALERT: AzureKeyVault prod-kv increased 5xx rate by 4.7% over baseline in last 15m. metric=vault_requests_5xx threshold=1.5% rule=kv-error-spike

dan.infra: Rollback completed at 1769990120 UTC. Verified that managed identities can auth again and 403s dropped to baseline. I opened a follow-up PR to add a staged rollout for RBAC changes + runbook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/432 (contains verification script + canary checks).

dan.infra: I also added a short-term mitigation branch that:
- sets dek_local_cache_ttl_seconds default to 300
- enables client-side jittered backoff
- instruments a fallback counter metric 'crypto.dek_fallback_count'

maria.security: Thanks — next steps for incident/near-miss handling:
- dan please own the post-incident summary and link all telemetry (logs / metrics / blob exports).
- oliver please own the short-term mitigations and add the circuit-breaker defaults to the KV client library.
- anyya.prod (compliance) please confirm what exact retention format you need for SOC2 evidence.

anya.prod: We need a CSV with: timestamp, request_id, key_id, outcome{decrypt|fallback|error}, actor_identity, and blob_sha256. Retain exported audit logs for 90 days. Confirmed.

leo.ops: I'll produce an initial impact estimate: approx 120k decrypt attempts during the 12-minute window, ~8.4k failed first-attempts, ~7.2k served via fallback DEK cache. Will attach metric graphs to the postmortem.

maria.security: Good. Let's keep the thread for action items only. I'll create the incident doc and link the artifacts once dan's export finishes. :white_check_mark:

dan.infra: Export job kicked off to secure-s3 at 1769990200 (job id export-azkv-1769990200). Will update when complete.

oliver.sre: Note for postmortem: consider adding a KV quota-aware throttle (per-key QPS limiter) and a safe default to disable automatic wide RBAC revokes without canary.

maria.security: Assigning timeline/owner: dan (postmortem + PR), oliver (client circuit + deploy), leo (impact numbers + graphs), anya (SOC2 evidence checklist). We'll reconvene in the postmortem doc.

kms-bot: NOTE: Export job export-azkv-1769990200 completed successfully at 1769990345. Files: s3://redwood-sec-exports/azkv/1769990200/*.log

maria.security: Closing thread here — thanks all. We'll mark this as a near-miss and run the full RCA next week.
